'''Edward Thomas Copson''' [[FRSE]] (21 August 1901 – 16 February 1980) was a British [[mathematician]] who contributed widely to the development of mathematics at the [[University of St Andrews]], serving as [[Regius Professor of Mathematics]] amongst other positions.

==Life==
He was born in [[Coventry]], and was a pupil at [[King Henry VIII School, Coventry|King Henry VIII School]], Coventry. He studied at [[St John's College, Oxford]]. He was appointed by [[E. T. Whittaker]] as a lecturer at the [[University of Edinburgh]], where he was later awarded a DSc.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Copson/|title=Edward Copson - Biography|website=[[mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk]]|access-date=30 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Copson|first=E. T.|date=1928|title=Some problems in the theory of the partial differential equations of mathematical physics|url=https://era.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/30948|language=en|website=Era.ed.ac.uk}}</ref>

He married Beatrice, the elder daughter of [[E. T. Whittaker]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/newsletter/322/322_03.html |title=Untitled Document |access-date=2010-02-22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20050215045321/http://www.lms.ac.uk/newsletter/322/322_03.html |archive-date=15 February 2005 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> and moved to the University of St Andrews where he was  [[Regius Professor of Mathematics]], and later dean of science, then Master of the United College. He was instrumental in the construction of the new Mathematics Institute building at the university.{{citation needed|date=August 2012}}

He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1924, his proposers being Sir [[Edmund Taylor Whittaker]], [[Herbert Stanley Allen]], [[Bevan Braithwaite Baker]] and [[Alexander Crichton Mitchell|A. Crichton Mitchell]]. He was awarded the [[Keith Medal]] by the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1942 for his research in mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Extras/Copson_Professor.html |title=Copson Professor |access-date=2010-02-22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607140306/http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Extras/Copson_Professor.html |archive-date=7 June 2011 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> He served as the Society's vice president from 1950 to 1953.<ref>
[https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/...index/fells_indexp1.pdf] {{dead link|date=September 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Work==
Copson's primary focus was in [[classical analysis]], [[asymptotic expansions]], [[differential equations|differential]] and [[integral equations]], and applications to problems in theoretical physics. His first book ''"The theory of functions of a complex variable"'' was published in 1935.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Copson.html |title=Copson biography |access-date=26 November 2007 |archive-date=13 August 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070813195906/http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Copson.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
